Join us and take the first step toward shaping the future of Citi!

jobs.title: Summer Congressional Internship Program at Congressional Hispanic Caucus Institute (CHCI)
jobs.description: Employer: Congressional Hispanic Caucus Institute (CHCI) Expires: 09/14/2026 With CHCI’s paid internships offered during the Summer and Fall, students can apply for the program that best fits their college timeline and schedule. CHCI interns will meet accomplished leaders, including CHCI Alumni, dedicated to improving the Latino community. These leaders come from a wide range of professional backgrounds, including Capitol Hill, Fortune 500 companies, NGOs, nonprofits, and other organizations that support Latino education and leadership development. The Congressional Internship Program (CIP) equips participants with legislative knowledge, cultural competency, an extensive network, and personal and professional leadership skills. CHCI interns come to D.C. from throughout the country. They will meet fellow Latinos from different heritages and backgrounds, learning as much from each other as from CHCI. As they work together, serve the community, and explore the nation’s capital, interns will build bonds that will last beyond the program. Interns will attend weekly programming sessions centered on CHCI’s four Pillars of Leadership: Self Discovery, Transformation through Collective Power, Rooted in My Strength, and Planting Seeds for Tomorrow. The CHCI pillars provide the support needed to strategize and produce organized, culturally relevant programming with timely content to create opportunities, transform, influence, and connect the next generation of Latino leaders. APPLY NOW PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS Attend an 8-day orientation and weekly leadership development sessions throughout the program Work a minimum of 32 hours a week in congressional office assignment Participate in all CHCI-sponsored activities including Hispanic Heritage Month events, Summits, and receptions Complete community service hours Comply with CHCI policies regarding work performance and personal conduct PROGRAM BENEFITS Congressional office internship placement Great Pay: $4,776 Domestic round-trip transportation to Washington, D.C. Medical insurance during the program (all premiums paid by CHCI) Furnished housing (rent and utilities covered) Academic credit (we encourage participants to discuss this with their academic advisors) $100 per month metro stipend Weekly leadership development training Exclusive networking opportunities PROGRAM ELIGIBILITY Students must be enrolled full time and working towards their undergraduate degree in the academic period before participating. Recent graduates who graduate in the term immediately prior to the program session may apply. Applicants must be enrolled full time during Spring 2027 and/or Summer 2027 (Summer enrollment not required). Eligibility for graduates is limited to those completing their degree in the summer. High academic achievement (preference of 3.0 GPA or higher) Evidence of leadership skills and potential for leadership growth Demonstrated commitment to public service-oriented activities Superior analytical skills, outstanding oral and written communication skills If selected as a finalist, all individuals will be required to provide proof of enrollment to participate in the program Community college individuals graduating in June are eligible for the summer session if they are transferring to a 4-year institution come the Fall semester. If selected, they will be required to provide confirmation of enrollment at new institution for the Fall semester Applicants must be U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, asylees, or individuals who are lawfully authorized to work full-time without restriction for any U.S. employer and who, at the time of application, possess lawful evidence of employment authorization. International students on F-1 or M-1 visas are not eligible for CHCI programs. NOTE: Individuals who are seeking consideration under the “Deferred Action for Childhood Arrival” (DACA) policy must be eligible to work and possess valid employment authorization at the time of acceptance and must maintain continuous lawful employment authorization for the duration of the program for which the person is applying. SELECTION PROCESS The selection process is competitive, consisting of two stages: A written application An asynchronous interview. Written applications and prerecorded interviews are reviewed by a selection committee composed of program alumni, members of the CHCI Board of Directors and Advisory Council, and CHCI staff.

jobs.title: Designer at Moglea
jobs.description: Employer: Moglea Expires: 09/14/2026 Position: Designer 8/14/26IN-PERSON POSITION - Part - Time - 20 hours weeklyWe're seeking a part-time Designer to join our Design Team. The Design Team is responsible for various creative aspects of the Moglea brand. Applicants should have a design-focused educational background with knowledge of programs like Photoshop, InDesign, and Illustrator. Experience with video and social media is a plus. Responsibilities include but are not limited to, designing engaging email campaigns, editing images, assisting in planning and producing social media content, and shooting video footage. Our Design Team also assists our creative directors with designing new products for the Moglea line. Our Design Team also plans and coordinates marketing efforts for the brand. We’re looking for someone who is organized, flexible, and ready to bring fresh ideas to the Moglea brand.Our Company: Moglea was launched in 2012 and is under the creative direction of Chad and Meg Gleason. Their artful stationery and product line is created by using hand-applied production processes to add one-of-a-kind elements to each product. The production team in their Des Moines, Iowa-based studio thoughtfully applies layers of paint to extra-thick sheets of paper before cutting them down, yielding completely unique compositions. Each piece is finished on one of their antique presses where it is foil stamped, printed, or die-cut using traditional letterpress printing processes. The Moglea line is a joyful exploration of composition, pattern and color. For each new release, Chad and Meg intentionally focus on adding unexpected production processes or visual ideas to the current collection. The result is a product line in which each piece feels like a work of art that is meant to be shared. The Moglea line is sold worldwide, with placement in over 1000 stores. The line has been sold nationwide by retailers such as Anthropologie, West Elm, CB2, Nordstrom, and Blick Art Materials. Our ValuesSincerity: We speak honestly and from our heart. We believe in caring personally and challenging directly as a means to improve performance when working together. We share our own stories and extend space for others to share theirs. We truly think this is the best and only way we can continue to grow as a team and company. Accountability: We embrace mistakes and learn together. We listen, observe, and gather information that brings us closer to understanding our team. We take responsibility for mistakes and create solutions for how to improve. Respect: We respect and listen to all members of our team, whether new to Moglea or senior employees. We respect and value the mission of the Moglea organization and the decisions our founders make toward that vision. Empathy: We desire to truly know and understand all members of our team - their points of view, their motivations, and their personal feelings. We desire to match our team’s strengths and skills to roles that can make the most impact. Our understanding of others will help build sustainable and productive relationships that help improve the corporate intimacy within the culture at Moglea. Humility: We recognize that we can, and we will be wrong. New information, time, and new levels of understanding ask us to challenge our previously held opinions and seek to improve ourselves and our work. We will be open to feedback from our peers, those above us, and our direct reports. We will self-reflect on recent decisions and motivations. Adaptive Tenacity: We passionately commit to our goals and stick to that commitment with a spirit of open-hearted and earnest striving and life-long learning. We are growth-minded and ask that all employees continue to grow and adapt to the growth of our company. We seek to accomplish higher performance levels, improved communication, and stronger relationships with all Moglea employees. Integrity: We ask that all Moglea employees are trustworthy, do what is right, and lead by example. Ownership: We don’t wait for others to act. We take the initiative to bring about positive results. We ask that employees care about Moglea products, processes, property, and personnel just as much as an owner of the company would. Taking ownership means we are accountable for the results of our actions and that they are executed with the highest quality and in a timely manner. Joy: We acknowledge that as coworkers, we see each other more than family and friends. Work can be challenging but overall should be fun, joyful, and fulfilling to every member of the Moglea team. We seek to ensure that every employee has a net positive experience while working at Moglea. Primary duties:• Maintaining the aesthetic quality of the Moglea brand. • Designing work such as email campaigns and social media content. • Plan and execute sales and marketing campaigns. • Collect market research, identifying potential markets and testing. • Editing and preparing images for use across various platforms. • Updating shop and social media platforms with fresh content. • Shooting and editing video footage of the production team. • Assisting the Design Team with other tasks as assigned. • Planning and brainstorming new ideas for video content. • Designing brand collateral for the Moglea brand. • Developing new color palettes and mood boards for each collection. • Designing brand collateral for the Moglea Furniture line. • Developing new production processes and assisting with process execution within the studio. • Assisting with production as needed for large orders or during busy times. • Stocking and merchandising the DSM retail shop. • Assisting with events within the retail shop. • Assisting customers within the retail shop. • (potential / growth in role) - Designing products and packaging for Moglea Paper line.Desired Education/Experience/SkillsAdobe Suite, especially Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign and Premier Pro. Instagram / Social media. Experience with shooting and editing video is required. Must have the ability to use basic video editing apps like CapCut, Edits and Premier Pro. Position Type: Part-time. In Person. Starting Pay Range: The pay range will be from 40-45K annual base salary with benefits. The pay range will be $ 20- $ 26 per hour for part-time positions. Our full-time Design positions are salary positions with benefits (HRA, retirement savings, paid vacation and sick days, employee discount, free downtown parking spot, Friday happy hour, Staff Lunches.) Our initial package is 10 paid days, 7 paid holidays, 3 paid sick days, and 10 days of parental leave. lBenefits:• Flexible schedule - We can accommodate any schedule between 6 AM-7 PM, Monday through Friday. • Free cards. • Relaxed work environment. • Ability to learn and grow within a creative environment. Location:Our production studio is downtown Des Moines at 110 11th Street, Des Moines, IA 50309. Equal Opportunity Employer: We are an equal employment opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Application Process:Please email jobs@moglea.com and submit:Your cover letter, resume (if you have one or just a listing of job history if applicable), and a portfolio link or PDF. Your cover letter should state why you think you would be a great fit at Moglea or why you would like to work at Moglea. Please also put the position you are applying for in the subject line of your email - DesignerWe appreciate you taking the time to consider yourself for this position. If you have any questions, please email jobs@moglea.com.

Assisting with external oversight and engaging in outreach activities pertinent to informing ratepayers of proposed tariff modifications, public information on consumer assistance, energy savings/efficiency programs, Long Island’s clean, renewable, and distributed energy resources, and annual Utility 2.0 and Energy Efficiency Plans\Assisting in collecting and analyzing data relevant to assessing the adequacy of existing and/or proposed metrics to determine their efficiency and effectiveness at achieving program targets and deliverables. Reviewing and summarizing the public comments of Long Island residential/commercial ratepayers and assisting in developing Department responses. jobs.description: Employer: Southern Hospitality Internship Program (SHIP) Expires: 09/16/2026 THE ROLEGreat Big Game Show Hosts are world-class hospitality experts who genuinely love people, thrive in high-energy environments, and take pride in creating unforgettable guest experiences.As a Host, you’ll lead guests through our live, hour-long game show experiences, where teams compete in 8-10 fast-paced mini-games involving physical challenges, trivia, luck, and skill. You’ll introduce each game, deliver fun commentary, track points, and ultimately crown a winning team, all while making every guest feel seen, celebrated, and included. Check out this video to see what it’s all about!Our Internship program offers an opportunity to learn more of the behind the scenes operations that go into running a dynamic and fast-growing retail-entertainment business. This would look like fast-tracking into a team leader position and joining our internal leadership development course led by our Director of Operations. You would gain hands-on management experience leading shifts of 3-5 team members and learning what it’s like to lead and motivate a team. This is a guest-facing, performance-based role where energy, confidence, and care for others matter. Hosts set the tone for the entire experience, from the first introduction to the final celebration. People who do best here are naturally hospitable, coachable, and energized by making someone else’s day better.WHY AN INTERNSHIP?Fast track into Team Leader in Training role, where you’ll develop concrete management experience, retail sales and hospitality skillsReal world business leadership development course from our Director of OperationsPost Grad management opportunities for those who excelA really fun way to complete an internship credit!WHAT YOU’LL DO Guest Experience & HostingLead groups of 2-14 guests through live game showsDeliver upbeat, conversational introductionsIntroduce each mini-game clearly and enthusiasticallyImprovise fun, family-friendly commentary for guests of all agesTrack points, award winners, and celebrate with guestsDeliver a clear, engaging outro recap of the experienceResolve service failures immediately and graciouslyCheck in guests for their game show and prepare them for fun!Operations & Team SupportUse Host software and studio UI to operate game showsEnsure studios are reset accurately and efficiently using setup sheetsLead the team on your shift with excellence and enthusiasm Manage cash and POS system as well as assist in inventory managementSchedule breaks for the team on shiftMaintain excellent time management to stay on schedule for assigned games GROWTH & CAREER PROGRESSION This Internship Program is designed with clear opportunities for growth. High level students that are selected for this program will grow in skill, consistency, and leadership, which could lead to opportunities including:Pay increases tied to performance and positional changesTraining certifications and advanced management responsibilitiesAdvancement into higher level leadership roles We believe in transparent expectations. Growth comes from excellent hospitality, alignment with Mission, Vision and Values, teamwork, a positive attitude, and mastery of the current role you are in. We promote based on Performance, Availability and Commitment. Team members who excel in these areas can grow very quickly!Team members that excel can grow as quickly as:Assistant Manager In Training: 3-9 monthsAssistant Manager: 6-12 monthsFurther growth can lead to a GM role either in your current store or relocating to a new location, as GBGS opens new stores across the country! QualificationsREQUIREMENTSFlexible availability, including nights, weekends, and holidaysAbility to stand and host for extended periods (up to 4-5 game shows per shift)Comfort with extended public speaking and guest interactionAbility to improvise appropriate, professional commentaryStrong verbal communication skillsAbility to perform physical tasks such as cleaning, lifting 30-40 lbs, bending, crawling, painting, and minor repairsAbility to reset game components within specific timeframesAlignment with GBGS Uniform Standards (Click HERE to view the uniform standards)KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES Genuine love for serving othersCoachability, humility, and a team-first mindsetPublic speaking and communication skillsQuick decision-making and creative problem-solvingBasic computer and technology skillsComfort working in a fast-paced, guest-focused environmentLeadership and professionalism Please note: This role and many others are offered through the Southern Hospitality Internship Program, a local government nonprofit program for multiple businesses and internships near Gatlinburg, TN. All roles include competitive pay, housing, networking events, and a leadership track.Learn more: https://southernhospitalityinternshipprogram.com/

jobs.title: Summer Associate, Client Service, San Francisco, 2027 at AlphaSights
jobs.description: Employer: AlphaSights Expires: 09/16/2026 Location: San FranciscoStart date: June 7, 2027End date: August 13, 2027Duration: 10 weeksLooking for an internship with commercial frontline responsibility and the opportunity to work on live client projects? Do you seek to have immediate personal impact? If so, our Summer Associate program is the right choice for you.About AlphaSightsWe bring together some of the most ambitious people from around the globe to work with the leading investment funds, strategy consultancies and Fortune 500 companies. Together, we help our clients access expert knowledge, elevate their decision-making and drive progress by connecting them with niche experts across the world.Founded in 2008, our journey has been nothing short of extraordinary. With 2,000+ professionals in nine cities worldwide, we’ve earned our place as a leader in our market through our client service excellence, and integrating our proprietary technology to stay ahead of the curve. Our relentless pursuit of excellence means we only hire the best and brightest graduates to help us reach new heights.Consider the Summer Associate program if:You thrive in a fast-paced, results-oriented environment.You possess a client-first mindset.You excel under pressure and enjoy using tech-enabled workflows to meet tight deadlines.You are gritty, resilient and ready to roll up your sleeves to make things happen.You enjoy the opportunity to regularly upskill on new tools and workflows, including those powered by AI, to improve your professional output.A day in the life of a Summer AssociateAs a Summer Associate in the Client Service team, you’ll be the link between our clients and the expert knowledge they seek. These connections could take the form of an hour-long phone call between the client and expert advisor, a survey, or a written research product. Throughout your workday, you will work on multiple projects from investors, strategists and dealmakers at top-tier client organizations seeking expert insights to inform their decision-making. This is a communications-intense frontline role requiring you to multitask across parallel workstreams.Your responsibilities will include:Owning end-to-end client-expert communications, spending a significant part of your day on the phone screening and negotiating with relevant experts to position the best possible matches for your clients’ requests.Leveraging AI-powered sourcing tools to map complex industry value chains and identify and engage with relevant experts.Understanding the project and market context and the legal and regulatory environment in which your clients and experts operate.Ensuring success for our Summer Associates means:Giving you an introduction to the business world without being pigeonholed into any one industry or profession.Helping you develop transferable commercial and client management skills spanning professional communications, negotiation, persuasion, project and time management.A unique training curriculum and intense on-the-job coaching, helping you develop highly transferable commercial and managerial skills.An inspiring, high-energy, merit-based environment with ambitious peers.RequirementsYou’ll need to bring your A game to work, daily. We are looking for:Undergraduate Junior (Class of 2028). Strong academic credentials (undergraduate GPA of 3.3 or above).Noteworthy extracurricular achievement throughout school and university.Internship experience evidencing an interest in business is a plus.Fluent English is required.Work authorization in the United States; we do not sponsor visas but will consider applicants with STEM/OPT eligibility.BenefitsInternship compensation is $15,384.62 for a 10-week program.Opportunity to receive a full-time employment offer to return post-graduation. Learn more about our commercial career paths here.State-of-the-art office with amenities in the heart of San Francisco; option to WFH each Friday.AlphaSights is an equal-opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Founder's Office GTM Intern at Fenix Commerce Inc
jobs.description: Employer: Fenix Commerce Inc Expires: 09/16/2026 Company Description FenixCommerce is an AI-powered, end-to-end delivery management platform that helps eCommerce retailers reduce shipping costs by 10–25% and increase conversion rates by up to 40%. Founded by experienced eCommerce professionals, the company focuses on enabling retailers to compete with large marketplaces by elevating their delivery experience. The platform supports the entire delivery journey, from accurate pre-purchase estimated delivery dates and multi-carrier rate shopping to intelligent order routing with inventory visibility. FenixCommerce also provides branded shipment tracking to keep retailers’ brands prominent after purchase and significantly reduce “where is my order” support inquiries. The company is committed to helping brands and shippers ship smarter, deliver better, and grow profitably. Role Description The Founder’s Office – Growth and Ops Intern is a full-time, on-site role based in San Jose, responsible for supporting strategic growth initiatives and operational excellence across the organization. This role involves partnering closely with the founder to drive growth projects, coordinate cross-functional execution, and track key business metrics. Daily responsibilities include managing workflows and operations, preparing analytical reports and presentations, and supporting customer-facing initiatives that improve delivery experience and adoption of the FenixCommerce platform. The position also includes handling administrative tasks, overseeing documentation and basic financial processes, and collaborating with teams such as Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Marketing to ensure smooth internal communication and efficient service delivery. The individual will be expected to proactively identify process improvements, assist in planning and execution of special projects, and act as a central point of coordination for the founder’s priorities. QualificationsStrong communication skills, including clear written and verbal communication and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and senior leadership.Administrative assistance and office administration skills, including organizing schedules, managing documentation, coordinating meetings, and maintaining efficient office processes.Customer service capabilities, with experience supporting client-facing teams, responding to inquiries professionally, and contributing to a positive customer experience.Basic accounting and financial administration skills, such as handling expense tracking, invoice coordination, and supporting budget or reporting tasks.Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, prioritize tasks, and work independently in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with comfort using spreadsheets, dashboards, and data to inform decisions and track performance metrics.Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations, Commerce, or a related field; prior experience in eCommerce, logistics, SaaS, or startup environments is an advantage.High level of integrity, ownership mindset, and willingness to work closely with founders on strategic and operational initiatives.How to apply:to be considered for this role, send a self recorded video and your resume to akhilesh@fenixcommerce.com. LI applications won't be considered.

jobs.title: Marketing Intern (B2C) at Fastflo
jobs.description: Employer: Fastflo Expires: 09/16/2026 Marketing Intern, B2C Growth & UGCFastflo | Remote (Cambridge, MA, hybrid welcome) | Part-time or Full-time | PaidAbout FastfloFastflo is a hyper-growth B2B SaaS startup built at the Harvard Innovation Labs. We're changing how companies hire frontline workers: instead of forcing candidates through clunky web forms, applications happen natively inside WhatsApp and iMessage. Around 80% of candidates finish their application, versus roughly 15% on traditional flows. We recently closed our seed round, and we're now launching something new: a job board built for candidates.That job board needs to be everywhere candidates are. That's your job.The RoleYou will own consumer marketing for our job board launch. Not "support" it, not "assist with" it. Own it. You'll be the person responsible for getting job seekers to discover us, and you'll have real freedom in how you do it.We do things very differently at Fastflo, and that's why we win. We're not looking for someone to schedule three polished posts a week. We're looking for someone with the creative instincts and the nerve to run guerrilla plays that bigger companies would never approve: content that gets shared, stunts that get talked about, ideas that punch far above our budget.And we're not hiring for a semester. We're hiring the person who could lead marketing at Fastflo. This internship is how you earn that: prove it and the intention is to convert you into a long-term position with real ownership of the function as we scale.What You'll DoCreate UGC yourself: short-form video for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts about job searching, careers, and our job boardBuild a machine for getting others to create UGC: creator partnerships, campus ambassadors, challenges, whatever worksRun our candidate-facing social channels and grow them from scratchInvent and execute guerrilla campaigns to drive job seekers to the boardTrack what's working and double down ruthlesslyWhat Success Looks LikeJob seekers discovering and signing up for the job board. You'll have clear growth targets, full ownership of the channels, and a direct line to the founders. When your video hits, everyone will know it was yours.Who Thrives HereCurrently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor's or master's degreeYou already make content, or you've been itching for an excuse to startA ton of initiative: you generate ideas without being asked and ship them without hand-holdingComfortable on camera, or great at getting other people to beScrappy: you see a $0 budget as a creative constraint, not an obstacleNo formal marketing experience required. Taste, energy, and output matter more.Compensation & LogisticsPaid position with performance incentives tied to growth resultsAcademic credit available where your program allows, in addition to compensationRemote by default; you're welcome to join us in person or hybrid in Cambridge if you're localPart-time or full-time depending on your availabilityThis role is designed to convert: perform well and you move into a long-term position with a path to leading marketing at Fastflo

As the accrediting body for public health in the United States, PHAB advances standards of excellence and accountability for the systems that promote and protect the health of all people. The Hourly Project Assistant II will assist with the review of the State Health Department’s submitted PHAB Required Documentation. This review seeks to identify documents that New York State (NYS) LHDs can utilize for their respective accreditation or reaccreditation. Valid and unrestricted authorization to work in the U.S. is required. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. Travel up to 10% of the time will be required. jobs.title: Development & Communications Intern at LIFT Inc
jobs.description: Employer: LIFT Inc Expires: 09/17/2026 POSITION: Development & Communications Intern LOCATION: National REPORTS TO: Director, Individual GivingSUPERVISES: N/AFLSA STATUS: NonexemptHOURLY RATE: $22TRAVEL, TIME COMMITMENT & Duration:Local In-Person External Meetings: 0%20-25 hours per month through December 31, 2026 with the possibility of extensionABOUT OUR ORGANIZATION LIFT is on a mission to break the cycle of poverty by investing in parents. Through direct work with families, engaging technical assistance partnerships, and by advocating for policies that drive systemic change, we’re fighting poverty by lifting two generations at once. Our team culture is rooted in deep respect for the parents we partner with and for each other. We’re looking for dedicated team members who share our vision that, 25 years from now, LIFT is no longer needed because we have helped build a social service system grounded in Hope, Money, and Love, where all families can thrive. We’re guided by mission- and strategy-aligned leadership grounded in kindness, curiosity, relationships, and a commitment to equity. Explore our benefits and what it’s like to work at LIFT below –or download our Benefits & Culture Overview to learn more.*LIFT operates sites in Chicago, Los Angeles, DC, and New York. This position may be done remotely from any state where LIFT currently operates.POSITION OVERVIEW This is a part-time internship requiring approximately 20 hours per month through December 31, 2026, with the possibility of extension. This role will report to the Director, Individual Giving, and will work closely with the Communications Manager. This part-time Development & Communications intern will support LIFT’s fundraising-focused communications efforts and external-facing communications. The internship is writing-driven, with responsibility for developing donor-facing communications, social media, and organizational content, creating compelling stories and content that engage supporters, strengthen relationships, advance fundraising goals, and broaden LIFT's reach and visibility.AS THE DEVELOPMENT & COMMUNICATION INTERN YOU WILL… DevelopmentDraft and edit donor-facing communications and development content that engage supporters, communicate impact, and strengthen relationships with donors and partners. Create and refine templates and adaptable content that can be used across multiple cities, ensuring consistency while tailoring messaging for local contexts.Support the development and execution of fundraising-focused communications strategies that effectively engage and retain donors.Develop clear, concise, and compelling written content that reflects both local impact and a broader national perspective.Collaborate with internal stakeholders to gather input and ensure alignment on messaging, while working independently.Proofread and edit content with a high level of attention to detail, ensuring accuracy, clarity, and consistency in tone and branding across materials.Explore opportunities to enhance communication through visual storytelling, including basic graphic design and video content to support fundraising efforts.Support broader development and communications activities, including event preparation, coordination, and administrative support as neededCommunicationsManage LIFT's social media presence day-to-day — writing and building posts, maintaining a consistent content calendar, and adapting content across platforms.Support the writing and editing of external content including the monthly newsletter, blog posts, and the annual report.Copy edit across external materials, serving as a reliable second pair of eyes on accuracy, consistency, tone, and brand.Track relevant news, research, and field conversations to surface content opportunities.OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE Strong writing and editing skills, with the ability to produce clear, concise, and compelling content for a range of audiences, including donors, partners, and social media audiences.Experience or interest in development and fundraising communications, donor engagement, and mission-driven storytelling.Fluency with social media as a communications tool. Comfortable writing copy and creating content for LinkedIn, Instagram, X, and Facebook, and maintaining a content calendar.Ability to work independently in a remote, flexible environment.High attention to detail, including proofreading for accuracy, consistency, and grammatical correctness.Self-motivated with a willingness to learn and grow skills in areas such as fundraising strategy, graphic design, and multimedia content (e.g., video).Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to contribute to longer-term projects by managing timelines, tracking tasks, and meeting deadlines.LIFT’S COMPETENCIESAll LIFT employees embrace and demonstrate our organization-wide core competencies:Communication: You share information with relevant parties in a clear and timely manner; effectively engage with and present to others; and write and verbally communicate in a manner that conveys understanding of relevant information and issues.Accountability: You take responsibility for the quality and timeliness of work and achieve results with appropriate levels of oversight. You receive feedback in a constructive manner.Inclusiveness: You help create a work environment that appreciates diversity and encourages equity by treating others with respect, listening to, and demonstrating appreciation for others’ perspectives, and using culturally sensitive language.Teamwork: You work effectively with others throughout the organization and promote cooperation and commitment within your team to achieve goals and deliverables.Results-orientation: You focus on results and desired outcomes, keeping team and organizational goals in mind. You use sound planning to achieve goals and get the job done.Problem-solving: You take the initiative to solve problems. You exhibit resourcefulness, innovation, and adaptability to new situations.Don’t think you have everything for this role but are still interested? Please don’t hesitate to apply. We’d love to hear from you! LIFT is an equal opportunity employer and believes that diversity in all dimensions of the organization supports and bolsters the innovative thinking essential to its success and is committed to providing equal employment opportunity to all qualified applicants. LIFT’s goal is for our people to reflect the communities in which we live and serve and to ensure representation of people of color, those who identify as women, veterans, and individuals with disabilities in our organization. WHAT WE OFFER Hourly rate: $22/hour. LIFT’s compensation philosophy is to pay competitively for our non-profit sector and ensure equity across the organization. jobs.description: Employer: Bread for the World Expires: 09/17/2026 Bread for the World is a Christian advocacy organization urging U.S. decision makers to do all they can to pursue a world without hunger. Our mission is to educate and equip people to advocate for policies and programs that can help end hunger in the U.S. and around the world. In general, the main projects for the next gen organizing intern include: Support national and local organizing efforts by recruiting and engaging students and young adults in advocacy campaigns and events.Research and build relationships with student groups, faculty, chaplains, and community partners to grow Bread for the World's NextGen network.Help plan and coordinate campus events, such as film screenings, discussions, and advocacy activities.Connect students to trainings and leadership opportunities and support the development of Student Leadership Teams on campusWork on additional projects as requested.SKILLS/KNOWLEDGE REQUIRED:Passion for social justice, advocacy, and ending hunger and poverty.Strong interpersonal and communication skills. Interest in organizing, leadership development, or public policy.Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a remote environment.Experience with or willingness to learn outreach, event planning, and social media engagement.Current college student or recent graduate preferred.WORK ENVIRONMENT ISSUES:This internship can be based in Washington, DC or remote in PA.Bread is a hybrid organization. CULTURAL EXPRESSIONS:Bread is committed to advancing racial equity externally and internally, all staff members play a vital role. In the course of our work, each staff person should work to apply a racial equity lens to their work and practices; and participate in racial equity on-going training. Bread is also committed to being an equal opportunity employer.OUR VALUES:We value our faith. Our faith in Christ compels us to love our neighbors near and far and is the foundation for our hope, story, mission, and values.We value human flourishing. We believe that every human being, created in the image of God, has inherent dignity that affords an opportunity to thrive in relationship with God, self, neighbor, and the environment; and to access enough nutritious food for good health.We value justice. We seek to establish effective systems, structures, and policies that affirm equality and advance equity among all human beings to alleviate hunger and poverty.We value courage and prophetic voice. In a spirit of wisdom and love, we will be bold in articulating and pursuing our vision of a world without hunger.We value nonpartisanship. We believe that effective and sustainable public policies are made when, in good faith, we employ a civil and bipartisan approach to develop and implement laws and programs to achieve our mission.We value collaboration. We believe in working alongside and building community with a diversity of churches, interfaith communities, institutions, and individuals, including people experiencing hunger, to achieve our mission.We value impact. We strive for excellence in our work and hold ourselves and our nation’s leaders accountable in the pursuit of public policies that render measurable results and meaningful change for people everywhere affected by hunger.DISCLAIMER:Background and reference checks will be conducted on all final candidates. jobs.title: AI Talent Intern at Tenex
jobs.description: Employer: Tenex Expires: 09/17/2026 About TenexTenex is the next startup from co-founders Alex Lieberman and Arman Hezarkhani. Alex co-founded Morning Brew, which he built into one of the most recognized names in media before selling it to Business Insider, and with Tenex he and Arman are focused on helping companies put AI to work in ways that actually move the needle. We're the preferred partner of Anthropic, which means we operate at the frontier of what these tools can do and we bring that capability directly to our clients. It's a fast-moving, high-ownership environment where you'll work alongside people who are genuinely excited about building the future of AI-powered work. About the roleWe're hiring five sharp, curious interns to spend the summer at the intersection of AI and talent. You'll get hands-on exposure to how modern AI tools actually work, and you'll put them to use on a real problem: finding exceptional people. This isn't a fetch-coffee internship. You'll own a genuine sourcing mandate and have room to experiment with unconventional methods to reach candidates other recruiters miss. We're looking for standout students who have built or led something real. What you'll doLearn to use AI tools (LLMs, agents, automation) to research, identify, and evaluate candidates at scaleBuild and test creative, non-obvious sourcing strategies that go beyond the usual LinkedIn searchMine unconventional channels (communities, open-source projects, niche forums, events) to surface hidden talentDraft compelling, personalized outreach and track what actually gets responsesMaintain a clean candidate pipeline and share what's working with the teamPresent your findings and recommendations at the end of the summer Who you areA current college student with a strong academic recordResourceful and self-directed, someone who enjoys figuring things out and trying things others haven'tA clear writer and strong communicatorSomeone who has built or led something you're proud of, whether that's research, a startup-ish project, a hackathon, a club, or a teamComfortable being scrappy with new tools. No prior recruiting experience requiredAvailable in-person for the full internship period What you'll getReal ownership of a project with visible impactA crash course in applied AI you can't get in a classroomMentorship from the Tenex team and a portfolio of results to point toCompetitive pay

step out of comfort zone and take on new assignmentsDemonstrate a culture of ethical conduct, safety, and compliance; lead the team to work in the same way and hold others accountable to this commitmentWork in a safe manner at all times to benefit yourself and others; jobs.title: Pro Bono Innovations Fund Intern - Fall 2026 at Legal Services Corporation
jobs.description: Employer: Legal Services Corporation Expires: 09/18/2026 Position: Pro Bono Innovations Fund Intern Location: Washington, DC 20006Department: Office of Program Performance (OPP)Employment Status: Part-Time| Non-exempt | Hybrid | DC-Metro Area Only OVERVIEW:Established by Congress in 1974, the Legal Services Corporation (LSC) is the country’s single largest funder of civil legal aid for low-income Americans. LSC currently funds 129 independent legal aid offices nationwide. LSC’s mission is to promote equal access to justice and provide grants for high-quality civil legal assistance to low-income Americans.The Office of Program Performance (OPP) oversees LSC’s grantmaking and works with grantees to support high-quality legal services and effective program performance. Within OPP, the Pro Bono Innovation Fund (PBIF) supports innovative and effective approaches to expanding pro bono legal services. PBIF’s work includes grant administration, grantee support and technical assistance, program evaluation, research, and initiatives designed to strengthen and improve pro bono service delivery.The internships are based in Washington, DC, and will require working from an office in DC in accordance with LSC’s hybrid work model. The successful candidates must live in the DC metropolitan area for the duration of the internship. BASIC FUNCTION:The primary objectives of this internship are for the intern to:Develop a practical understanding of grantmaking, grant administration, program evaluation, and technical assistance within civil legal aid;Strengthen research, data analysis, professional writing, and presentation skills through substantive PBIF projects;Build experience reviewing grant applications, progress reports, supporting materials, and program data to identify trends, successes, challenges, and lessons learned;Strengthen project management, time management, professional communication, and effective workplace behaviors while supporting multiple projects;Gain hands-on experience using PBIF’s grant management, data tracking, and collaboration tools and processes.The internship is expected to run from September through December 2026. Interns will work part-time, up to 20 hours per week during the fall. PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:The intern's principal duties and responsibilities include:Supporting PBIF grant administration and reporting activities, including preparing progress report and payment request materials, reviewing reports for completeness, compiling data, and helping track reporting requirements and deadlines.Assisting with grantee communications and progress report preparation by reviewing grant applications, reports, and supporting materials; preparing materials for calls; tracking follow-up items; and participating in grantee meetings as appropriate.Conducting research and analysis related to PBIF grants, including reviewing past Sustainability grants and other grantee data to identify program successes, challenges, lessons learned, and opportunities for improvement.Supporting PBIF program evaluation activities by organizing and preparing information for external evaluators, assisting with data collection and analysis, and supporting related communications and data transfers.Assisting with the development of curriculum, workshops, presentations, visualizations, internal reference tools, and other resources for PBIF initiatives, including the PBIF Incubation grantee class and PBIF Grantee Meeting.Supporting planning and preparation for PBIF meetings, trainings, and events, including researching topics, organizing materials, assisting with logistics, and preparing supporting resources.Reviewing, organizing, and updating grant-related data and records using systems such as GrantEase, Smartsheet, Microsoft Excel, and other OPP tools.Drafting and editing templates, checklists, correspondence, presentations, reports, and other materials that support PBIF grant administration and program improvement.Participating in PBIF team and stakeholder meetings, taking notes, tracking action items, and coordinating follow-up activities with PBIF staff.Assisting with other OPP and PBIF projects and duties as assigned. WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:We are accepting applications from current undergraduate, graduate, and law students, as well as recent graduates of post-secondary institutions.The ideal applicant must be:Organized and attentive to detail;Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint;Strong in research, data analysis, written communication, and verbal communication;Comfortable reviewing detailed information, organizing data, and managing multiple assignments and deadlines;Able to work independently and collaboratively, ask thoughtful questions, and communicate professionally with team members and stakeholders;Intellectually curious and interested in learning about grantmaking, program evaluation, technical assistance, and civil legal aid;Committed to LSC’s mission of promoting equal access to justice;Interest or background in law, public policy, nonprofit management, program evaluation, research, data analysis, grants administration, or related fields preferred;Bonus: Experience with Smartsheet, data visualization, data management, presentation development, or grant management systems. HOURLY RATE:This position pays $20 to $22 per hour, based on your education level and internship status. APPLICATION PROCESS:To apply, visit www.lsc.gov/about-lsc/careers. Please submit:A current résuméA cover letter explaining your interest in this internship and how your goals align with LSC’s mission Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. If you need accommodations during the application process, email jobapplicant@lsc.gov.LSC is an equal-opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Grant Writer Intern at Social Responsibility Through Me
jobs.description: Employer: Social Responsibility Through Me Expires: 09/18/2026 SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY THROUGH MEsrtme.org | Camden, NJ | info@srtmworks.orgPOSITION OPENSeptember 2026Grant Writer InternPaid Internship | Part-Time, Flexible | Remote-Friendly | September 2026 – May 2027 Position at a GlanceOrganizationSocial Responsibility Through Me (SRTM)Position TitleGrant Writer InternInternship PeriodSeptember 2026 – May 2027 (9 months)Hours Per Week15 hours/week — flexible scheduleLocationRemote work available; occasional in-person in Camden, NJ preferredStipend$3,000 for the full internship period (September–May)Performance Bonus$500 bonus available upon achievement of grant goalEligibilityCurrently enrolled college students (sophomore, junior, or senior preferred)Reports ToCEO / Development Director, Shaneka M. Boucher About Social Responsibility Through MeSocial Responsibility Through Me (SRTM) is a Camden, New Jersey nonprofit organization founded in 2010 with a mission to engage, employ, and empower youth and adults in underserved communities. Through afterschool enrichment programs, workforce development, and community partnerships, SRTM creates pathways to economic mobility for the families we serve. Our programs currently support over 700 youth and adults. iWe operate multiple afterschool sites across Camden City and County, and are in an active growth phase with a $1.6 million operating budget and a $315,000 fundraising goal for 2026–2027. This internship is a genuine opportunity to contribute to work that directly changes lives — and to build real, résumé-ready grant writing experience in the process. The OpportunitySRTM is seeking a motivated, detail-oriented college student to join our development team as a Grant Writer Intern for the 2026–2027 academic year. This is not a filing or data-entry internship. You will be doing real grant writing — researching funders, drafting narrative proposals, compiling application materials, and submitting grants on behalf of an organization whose work you will come to know deeply. By the end of this internship, you will have submitted a minimum of 5 grant applications to real funders, built a portfolio of professional writing samples, developed a working knowledge of the NJ philanthropic landscape, and gained hands-on experience in nonprofit development that most students don't access until their first professional job. Compensation & Bonus Structure BASE STIPEND$3,000Paid over the full internship period (September 2026 – May 2027). Disbursed in monthly installments of approximately $333/month.PERFORMANCE BONUS$500Awarded at the end of the internship period if the intern successfully submits all 5 assigned grant applications by their deadlines, with all required components complete and meeting SRTM's quality standard. Total PotentialA Grant Writer Intern who meets all goals can earn $3,500 total over the 9-month internship — $3,000 base stipend + $500 performance bonus. Payment terms: the base stipend will be issued as 1099 compensation. Interns are responsible for their own taxes. SRTM will issue the $500 bonus upon verification that all 5 applications were submitted on time and meet quality standards as determined by the CEO. Core ResponsibilitiesThe Grant Writer Intern is responsible for the following activities across the internship period: GRANT RESEARCH & CALENDAR MANAGEMENTResearch and identify grant opportunities aligned with SRTM's mission in youth development, workforce development, afterschool programming, and economic mobility.Verify funder eligibility requirements — geographic focus, organizational eligibility, program alignment, and award range — before recommending any grant for pursuit.Maintain SRTM's Grant Calendar tab: update deadlines, application status, assigned amounts, and notes for all grants in the pipeline.Provide the CEO with a bi-weekly pipeline update identifying grants due in the next 60 days and any action items requiring CEO input. GRANT WRITING & APPLICATION PREPARATIONDraft full grant narratives for a minimum of 5 grant applications across the internship period, working from SRTM's program data, impact reports, and the Fundraising SOP framework.Write clearly and compellingly for nonprofit funders — leading with outcomes and data, not activities; using Camden-specific community need data to contextualize SRTM's work.Compile all required application attachments: IRS determination letter, 990, board list, audited financials, organizational budget, and program one-pagers — from SRTM's Grant Ready Folder.Ensure all applications are submitted a minimum of 72 hours before the funder's deadline. No exceptions.Submit all applications through the funder's required portal or method, save confirmation receipts, and update the Grant Tracker the same day as submission. GRANT TRACKING & REPORTING SUPPORTUpdate SRTM's Grant Tracker within 24 hours of any grant activity — application submitted, funder contact made, award or decline received.Support the Development Director in preparing interim and final grant reports for active grants as assigned.Help compile program outcome data from SRTM's five dashboard trackers (Attendance, Behavior, Homework, Voucher, Manager) for use in grant applications and reports.Assist with writing thank-you letters and acknowledgments to funders upon grant awards. LEARNING & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENTParticipate in weekly check-in meetings with the CEO/Development Director (30 minutes, remote or in-person).Attend at least one NJ nonprofit or funder information session during the internship period (virtual attendance acceptable).Review and apply SRTM's Fundraising Standard Operating Procedures as the guide for all development activities.Provide written feedback at the midpoint and end of the internship on the experience, challenges, and suggestions for improvement. The 5-Grant Goal — What Success Looks LikeThe intern is responsible for submitting 5 complete, quality grant applications between September 2026 and May 2027. These will be selected collaboratively with the CEO from SRTM's Grant Calendar based on the intern's start date, funder deadlines, and available program data. Below is a sample of what the 5-grant portfolio might look like: #Funder (Sample)Ask AmountTarget DeadlineCategory1Turrell Fund (NJ)$15,000–$25,000Sept/Oct 2026Youth Development / Afterschool2Campbell Soup Foundation$10,000–$20,000Jan 2027Education / Community (Camden)3Claneil Foundation$5,000–$15,000Feb 2027General Operating / Youth4TD Charitable Foundation$10,000–$20,000Rolling 2027Education / Workforce5NJ DOE After3 or similar$20,000–$50,000Spring 2027Afterschool / Academic Support Final grant selections will be confirmed during the intern's first week based on actual funder deadlines, current Grant Calendar status, and SRTM's program data availability. The intern will not be expected to submit grants for which SRTM does not have the necessary supporting documentation. What We Are Looking For Required QualificationsCurrently enrolled as a college sophomore, junior, or senior (or recent graduate within 6 months of graduation)Strong written communication skills — ability to write clearly, concisely, and compellingly for a professional audienceDetail-oriented and highly organized — grant writing is unforgiving of errors and missed deadlinesSelf-directed and able to work independently with minimal supervision in a remote environmentComfortable with Google Workspace or Microsoft Office (Docs/Word, Sheets/Excel)Genuine interest in nonprofit work, social justice, youth development, or community economic developmentPreferred QualificationsCoursework or experience in nonprofit management, public policy, social work, communications, English, education, or a related fieldPrevious writing experience — journalism, academic research, persuasive writing, communications internship, or similarFamiliarity with grant writing or fundraising concepts (even from a class or volunteer experience)Knowledge of Camden, NJ or experience working in under-resourced communitiesAbility to visit SRTM's Camden site at least once during the internship period What You Will GainThis internship is designed to give you real professional experience — not make-work tasks. Here is what you will leave with: Portfolio of Real Work5 submitted grant applications to real funders — professional writing samples you can use in job applications and interviews immediately.Sector KnowledgeA working understanding of the NJ philanthropic landscape, including how community foundations, corporate foundations, and government funders make decisions.Nonprofit Operations ExperienceExposure to a real nonprofit's development systems, program data, and funding strategy — the behind-the-scenes work most students don't see until their first job.Professional MentorshipWeekly direct access to SRTM's CEO, who has 15+ years of experience in nonprofit leadership and community development in South Jersey.Letters of RecommendationStrong performers will receive a detailed, personalized letter of recommendation from the CEO upon completion of the internship.Professional NetworkConnections to SRTM's partner organizations, employer partners, and NJ nonprofit community — a network that takes most people years to build.Schedule, Location & Logistics Hours15 hours per week. The intern and supervisor will agree on a schedule during the first week. Hours are flexible and can be arranged around class schedules.Remote WorkThe majority of work can be completed remotely. Interns are expected to attend weekly virtual check-in meetings and may be asked to visit SRTM's Camden office occasionally for orientation, events, or collaborative sessions.Internship PeriodSeptember 2026 – May 2027. The intern is expected to complete the full internship period to receive the full stipend. Interns who leave before May 2027 will receive a prorated stipend based on months completed. The $500 bonus requires full completion.ToolsSRTM uses Google Workspace (Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive). All grant tracking, research, and writing will be conducted in shared Google documents. A personal laptop or computer with internet access is required.Academic CreditSRTM is happy to support academic internship credit requirements. The CEO will complete any required supervisor evaluations or forms needed by your institution. How to ApplySRTM welcomes applications from college students of all backgrounds, especially those with personal connections to Camden or communities like it. You do not need prior grant writing experience to apply — you need strong writing skills, curiosity, and the drive to do the work. #SubmitDetails1RésuméCurrent résumé — one page preferred. Include all relevant coursework, writing experience, volunteer work, or extracurriculars.2Writing SampleOne writing sample of your choice — ideally something persuasive, research-based, or analytical. Academic papers are fine. If you have any nonprofit or grant writing samples, include those.3Short Cover LetterNo more than one page. Tell us: why SRTM's mission connects with you, what writing experience you bring (any kind), and what you hope to learn from this internship. Be specific — generic cover letters are immediately apparent.4OptionalIf you have completed any grant writing courses, workshops, or have access to a sample grant application you have written, include it as a bonus attachment. Send Applications ToNicquera Allen: msnallen@srtme.orgApplication DeadlineRolling — applications reviewed as received. Priority consideration given to applications submitted by August 15, 2026. Internship begins September 2026.Questions?Reach out to Ms. Nicquera Allen directly at msnallen@srtme.org or 856-952-2574. SRTM is a small team and we respond to every inquiry personally. Equal Opportunity StatementSocial Responsibility Through Me is an equal opportunity organization. We actively welcome applications from students of color, first-generation college students, students from Camden and South Jersey, students with disabilities, and students who bring lived experience in the communities we serve. We believe the best grant writers for SRTM are those who understand our community from the inside.SRTM does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Engineering Intern at Polaris Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Polaris Inc. Expires: 09/19/2026 Internship Program Overview The Polaris Engineering Internship is a tailored 12-week paid summer internship designed for emerging juniors, and seniors who are interested in pursuing a career in a leading global powersports industry. This program is for future leaders who seek a culture built on innovation, passion, and collaboration. As an Engineering Intern, you will be given impactful, project-based assignments that allow you to have exposure to multiple facets of engineering so you will experience both larger ongoing projects as well as shorter-scale projects throughout the summer that align with our business objectives. You will be placed into a specific team based on interest and business needs. These teams could include, but are not limited to: Design Engineering Project Engineering Systems Engineering Test or Development Engineering Potential Placement Locations Could Include: Roseau, MN; Wyoming, MN; Huntsville, AL; or San Angelo, TX, Novi, MI As a Polaris intern it is important that you embrace the adventure and remain open to any placement opportunity. By being adaptable, you will gain diverse experiences and develop a broader skill set, which are essential for your professional development and success within Polaris. Our internship program is crafted to build the foundational skills and experiences essential for your career success. Upon completing the internship, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a strong passion for learning may be offered a returning internship or a position in our rotational leadership development program. In addition to meaningful project work, you will participate in intentional programming and professional development offerings such as: Mentorship: you are paired with one of our DP associates for mentor support throughout your 12-weeks. Programming Hours: weekly functional and centralized learning sessions to broaden your knowledge base, both within and beyond your program. Networking: intentional time with peers and leaders at Polaris to build your professional network. Intern Innovation Challenge: internal case study designed to promote cross functional development where you and your team will present creative and practical solutions to a real ‘Polaris’ problem to our executive leadership. Early Talent Summit Week: participate in our 3-day event in our Wyoming, MN office. This immersive experience brings together all US interns and DPs for professional development, structured networking, a DP graduation event, inspiring executive speakers, and a thrilling team ride on some of your favorite Polaris vehicles. Community Engagement: opportunity to get involved in your local community. Final Presentations: present to our senior level leaders to showcase your career aspirations and recap your internship experience. The Selection Process: Applications are open from August -November each year. Applications will be reviewed and shortlisted candidates will typically be contacted for an initial phone screen by the end of November. Candidates selected to move forward will be invited to participate in a virtual panel interview with an identified HR business partner and functional leader. Successful candidates would move forward to an offer. You will partner with the Early Talent team in January to complete a survey that provides a deeper look at your specific interests, strengths & career goals. All specific internship assignments are communicated in February, after aligning based on your specific interests and business demand. Intern Relocation Assistance: Polaris offers a relocation program for interns who qualify through our mobility vendor. To qualify for these services, your home address must be 35 miles or more from the office where you will be working. Benefits include a lump sum (grossed up to offset tax liability), access to a relocation counselor to explain the resources available to you and aid in securing short-term housing available to you. Your responsibilities will include daily transportation to and from the office. Required Qualifications: Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master's degree in Engineering (e.g. mechanical, electrical, computer, software, or systems engineering) with an intended graduation date between August 2027-May 2029. Minimum overall GPA of 3.0 Able to complete full 12-week internship working 40 hours per week within the dates: May 17th – August 6th, 2027. June 1st – August 20th, 2027. Willing and able to relocate. Must be a U.S. person (U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident, asylee, or refugee) and not require sponsorship for employment now or in the future. Must have reliable transportation for daily commuting to and from the office. Previous experience with Microsoft Office software tools (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams, and Word). Preferred Qualifications: Demonstrated strengths in analysis, creative problem-solving, communication, interpersonal relationships, self-motivation, and leadership. Strong interest in long-term career development and participation in leadership development programs. Previous leadership experience in work, organizations, or classroom. Completion of at least two years of university coursework Previous Internship/Co-op experience Previous experience using CAD or equivalent software (Creo highly desired) Hands-on engineering experience through prior internship or clubs (ex. SAE, Clean Snow) This is more than an internship - It's the beginning of your career with Polaris. We hope you're ready for the ultimate adventure!

Coursework or experience in business strategy, finance, or operations. Exposure to data analytics tools or programming languages Participation in case competitions, business simulations, or entrepreneurial ventures. jobs.title: Account Manager Intern 1 at POSH Cars
jobs.description: Employer: POSH Cars Expires: 09/19/2026 About POSHPOSH is a luxury vehicle subscription company built on a simple idea: people should be able to access premium vehicles without the long-term commitment, depreciation risk, or paperwork of ownership or a traditional lease. Members subscribe to a vehicle tier and get flexibility that a dealership or leasing company can't offer.Behind our customer-facing subscription model is our Fleet Partner program, where individuals and businesses supply vehicles into our fleet in exchange for consistent returns. Managing both sides of this, the customer relationship and the fleet partner relationship, is what keeps POSH running.We're a small, fast-moving team, which means interns here get real responsibility, not busywork.About the RolePOSH is hiring an Account Manager Intern for fall 2026 with potential extension based on performance and business needs. This role sits at the intersection of customer success and fleet partner management.Once a customer signs on with POSH, this person becomes their main point of contact. They'll manage the relationship through the life of the subscription, handle questions and issues, and make sure the customer has a good experience that leads to retention.On the other side, this person will also manage relationships with our Fleet Partners. Fleet Partners are the backbone of our fleet, and keeping them informed, satisfied, and issue-free is critical to our supply chain.This is not a shadowing role. The intern will own a portfolio of accounts and partners and be expected to run point on them independently, with support from the team.What You'll Be Responsible ForActing as the main point of contact for customers after the sale, through onboarding, active subscription, renewals, and any issues that come upOwning customer success metrics, including satisfaction, retention, payments and timely resolution of complaintsManaging day-to-day communication with Fleet Partners, including status updates, issue resolution, and answering questions about vehicle performance or paymentsMaintaining accurate and organized records of every account and partner interactionBuilding recurring reports on account health, customer status, and partner activity for leadership reviewSpotting patterns, whether it's a customer segment showing early churn signs or a partner with recurring vehicle issues, and escalating them before they become bigger problemsWorking cross-functionally with Sales, Operations, Billing, and Fleet teams to resolve issues that touch more than one departmentSupporting process improvements for how customer and partner accounts are tracked and managedHelping maintain dashboards or reporting tools that track key account and partner metricsWhat We're Looking ForCurrently pursuing an undergraduate degree, any majorPrior experience in sales, account management, customer success, or a similar client-facing role is preferredExcellent written and verbal communication, this role is customer-facing and requires professionalismStrong analytical skills and comfort working with data to identify trends and inform decisionsHigh attention to detail. Small errors in account records or reporting can have real downstream consequencesA strong sense of ownership. This is not a role where you wait to be told what to doProficiency in Excel, including comfort with formulas and organizing data. Experience with dashboards or reporting tools is a plusStrong time management and the ability to juggle multiple accounts and partners at onceA proactive, problem-solving mindsetComfortable working in a fast-paced, small-team environment where responsibilities can shiftWhat You'll GainDirect ownership over real customer and partner relationships from your first weeks, not simulated projectsExposure to both sides of the business, sales-adjacent customer success and operational fleet partner managementHands-on experience with reporting and data management that informs real business decisionsClose mentorship from a lean team where your work is visible and has direct impactA strong foundation for a career in account management, customer success, or operations

jobs.description: Employer: Armanino Expires: 09/19/2026 Armanino is proud to be Among the top 20 Largest Firms in the Nation and one of the Best Places to Work. We have a community of resources that are ready and willing to support your ideas, build your skills and expand your professional network. We want you to integrate all aspects of your life with your career. At Armanino, we know you don’t check-out of life when you check-in at work. That’s why we’ve created a unique work environment where your passions, work, and family & friends can overlap. We want to help you achieve growth by giving you access to a network of smart and supportive people, willing to listen to your ideas. You will gain hands-on experience working alongside professionals at all levels that will provide you with insight into the field of public accounting. Your internship will give you the same exposure to Armanino as our associate-level hires, while participating in interactive and engaging programming. During your time interning with us, you'll also have the opportunity to participate in trainings and activities to boost your skills and engagement. Start Date: January 3, 2028 Job Responsibilities Assist in the performance and documentation of audit procedures and preparation of workpapers to contribute to the completion of audit, review, and other engagements. Work as an individual contributor and as part of an engagement team to support client needs Interpret and analyze financial date and communicate all findings and issues to the engagement team Research and analyze pertinent client, industry, and technical matters Engage with client personnel, as well as the engagement team to develop further relationships Requirements Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future Current enrollment in a bachelor's or master’s program in business with an emphasis in accounting Preferred Qualifications Plan to complete 150 semester/225 quarter unit requirement for CPA licensure eligibility between December 2028 – August 2029 strongly preferred "Armanino" is the brand name under which Armanino LLP and Armanino Advisory LLC, independently owned entities, provide professional services in an alternative practice structure in accordance with law, regulations, and professional standards. Armanino LLP is a licensed independent CPA firm that provides attest services, and Armanino Advisory LLC and its subsidiary entities provide tax, advisory, and business consulting services. Armanino Advisory LLC and its subsidiary entities are not licensed CPA firms. Armanino provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, Armanino complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training. Armanino expressly prohibits any form of workplace harassment based on race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, genetic information, disability, or veteran status. Improper interference with the ability of Armanino employees to perform their job duties may result in discipline up to and including discharge. Armanino does not accept unsolicited candidates, referrals, or resumes from any staffing agency, recruiting service, sourcing entity, or third-party paid service at any time. Any referrals, resumes, or candidates submitted to Armanino or any employee or owner of Armanino without a pre-existing agreement signed by both parties covering the submission will be considered the property of Armanino and not subject to any fees or charges. For existing agreements, a role must be approved and open to external search; otherwise, unsolicited and unapproved submittals and referrals will be considered Armanino property and free of fees. In addition, Talent Acquisition is the sole point of contact, and contacting others in our organization without Talent Acquisition’s knowledge will result in termination of contract. Armanino has a robust offering of benefits, including: Medical, dental, visionGenerous PTO plan and paid sick timeFlexible work arrangements401K with Profit SharingWellness programGenerous parental leave11 paid holidays For positions based in San Francisco, consistent with the SF Fair Chance Ordinance, an arrest and conviction record will not automatically disqualify a qualified applicant from consideration. For Individuals who would be working within the City of Los Angeles, Armanino will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance To view our Consumer Notice at Collection for job applicants, please visit: https://www.armanino.com/terms/ccpa-employee-notice/

jobs.title: Sales & Marketing Intern at Boon Logic
jobs.description: Employer: Boon Logic Expires: 09/19/2026 Sales & Marketing InternLocation: Minneapolis, MN | Hours: ~20 hrs/week, flexible schedule | Pay: $20/hour + bonus for qualified meetings bookedAbout Boon LogicBoon Logic is a Minneapolis-based AI company building advanced machine learning technology for industrial and pharmaceutical applications. Our flagship solution, AVIS, uses AI-powered automated visual inspection to help pharmaceutical manufacturers inspect injectable products for defects, and is being deployed across the U.S. with organizations ranging from fast-growing companies to some of the largest pharmaceutical companies in the world.You'll be part of a fun, collaborative, in-person environment at our North Loop office in Minneapolis, working alongside PhDs, master's graduates, engineers, sales leaders, and other motivated professionals building and commercializing the latest in AI technology right here in Minneapolis.About the OpportunityWe're looking for a motivated Sales & Marketing Intern to work directly alongside our sales and go-to-market leadership team in Minneapolis. This is a hands-on role for someone interested in sales, marketing, startups, AI, or entrepreneurship. You'll help us identify new customers, build outbound campaigns, create marketing content, manage our sales pipeline, and generate new opportunities for the business.A major focus will be growing our outbound sales efforts. In addition to the $20/hour base compensation, you'll earn a bonus for qualified sales meetings you help book.What You'll Work OnResearch and identify prospective pharmaceutical customersFind and research key decision-makers within target companiesSupport email, LinkedIn, and other outbound sales campaignsHelp book qualified meetings for the sales team, with bonuses for meetings bookedAssist with CRM and sales pipeline managementSupport LinkedIn, email, and broader marketing campaignsHelp develop sales and marketing contentAssist with customer demos, industry events, and trade showsSit in on sales calls and customer meetingsWork directly with sales leadership on new go-to-market ideas and campaignsWho We're Looking ForWe care more about drive, curiosity, and willingness to learn than having a long resume. You might be a great fit if you:Are currently pursuing a degree in business, sales, marketing, entrepreneurship, communications, or a related fieldAre interested in startups, AI, technology, sales, or marketingAre confident communicating with new people, and proactive and comfortable figuring things outWant exposure to real customers and real sales opportunities where your performance can directly impact the companyCan work approximately 20 hours per week, with a mix of in-person and hybrid work, flexible around your class schedule and other commitmentsWhy Join?You'll get direct exposure to how a growing AI company goes to market, working alongside the people actually building the sales strategy, contributing to real campaigns, customer opportunities, meetings, demos, and marketing initiatives, not hypothetical intern projects.Interested? Reach out to Ronan@boonlogic.com with a brief introduction and your resume.
